newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar dips against yen but downside supported.
newsitem.headline: Dollar dips against yen but downside supported.

text.p: The dollar was fractionally easier against the yen at the end of Asian morning trade on Tuesday, but dealers said its downside looked well supported around 126.50 yen.
A Japanese bank dealer said U.S. funds sold the dollar from its highs around 126.80/85 yen in early trade, but the amount sold was not large.
He said there were large sell orders above 127.10 yen ahead of an options position around 127.30 yen.
"The options expiry is on May 1 so people want to sell the dollar at 127.10/20 yen. But if 127.30 is taken, there'll be stop-loss buying," he said.
"Japanese investors have to buy four to five yards (billion) from May 1 so it will be difficult for the dollar to come down below 126.00 yen," he added.
He said the lack of a specific reference to the yen's recent weakness as a shared concern in Sunday's Group of Seven (G7) communique could spur more dollar/yen buying.

"Maybe the Japanese think the G7 showed no concern about the yen weakness so they'll try 128.0-130.0 yen after Golden Week," he said, adding however, that Japanese authorities were likely to intervene if the dollar went above 128.0 yen.

A European bank dealer said the dollar showed a bid tone. But it was likely to make slower progress against the yen than the mark due to fears of renewed tensions if Japan's trade surplus with the United States widened.
The dollar was expected to be well contained between 1.7300-1.7350 marks and 126.50-126.90 yen during Asian trade.
Hong Kong dealers said trade was subdued with the bulk of activity seen in the sterling crosses.
Sterling/mark recovered from an overnight low of 2.8170 while sterling/Swiss franc was up from 2.3850.
